cards.intuition: Bi-encoder: no interaction. Cross-encoder: total interaction, no precomputation. ColBERT: encode separately at token level, interact cheaply at the end.

cards.intuition: Let the expensive teacher score training pairs once, then train a cheap student to copy those scores. Deploy the student, not the teacher.
cards.formula: student learns from teacher scores, not just hard labels

cards.intuition: Soft scores say which negatives were nearly relevant and by how much; hard labels flatten all of that into yes and no.
cards.formula: 0.91 vs 0.79 vs 0.03 carries the margin structure

cards.intuition: Teacher compute is paid once over a fixed training set; student compute is paid per query forever at a fraction of the price.
cards.formula: one offline batch job -> indefinite cheap serving

cards.intuition: Run the teacher on unlabeled queries from your real traffic and distill; the student learns your domain without a single human judgment.
cards.formula: teacher scores on domain queries -> student trained on them

cards.intuition: The student copies the teacher's systematic errors along with its skill, so audit the teacher before mass-producing its opinions, and never distill a distilled model.
